title: Set the annual budget & get board approval
summary: Turn last year’s actuals into next year’s operating plan: pull the numbers, draft the model and headcount plan, negotiate the trade-offs with department leads, and take the budget to the board for a signed consent.

parts.title: Pull the year’s actuals and runway
parts.guidance: Establish the budget baseline from year-to-date actuals, the remaining-year forecast, cash and current runway model. Align periods and reconcile headcount, revenue and major commitments to their schedules. Separate recurring costs from unusual items and label the rest of the year’s estimates. Department leads should begin planning from these consistent figures.

execution.rationale: Reconcile supplied actuals, forecast and runway schedules into a consistent budget baseline.

parts.title: Draft the operating model and headcount plan
parts.guidance: Model revenue, staffing dates, compensation, delivery costs and major purchases as monthly cash flows. Tie opening cash and headcount to actuals, and make the assumptions and formulas easy to inspect. Compare the base plan with a downside case so leadership can see which hires or spending choices change the funding requirement.

execution.rationale: Build a monthly operating and headcount model with inspectable assumptions and downside scenarios.

parts.title: Review trade-offs with department leads
parts.guidance: Discuss each department’s proposed spending against the outcomes it is expected to deliver. Identify essential hires and purchases, milestone-dependent commitments and deferrable work. Resolve overlapping requests and unfunded obligations within the company’s cash constraints, then reflect the agreed trade-offs and decision triggers in the operating model.

execution.rationale: Department leads and leadership agree spending tradeoffs and commitments; the discussion medium is unspecified.

parts.title: Circulate the budget deck to the board
parts.guidance: Circulate the budget deck and model to the authorized board audience with the proposed plan, cash scenarios and decisions requested. Explain why management prefers this plan and where alternatives remain open. The company’s board coordinator should check document access and collect directors’ questions for the discussion.

execution.rationale: Google Slides is retained, but the distribution method, document-access checks and collection of directors' questions are unspecified. Gmail's send operation alone does not establish the full workflow.

parts.title: Board reviews and discusses the plan
parts.guidance: Use the board discussion to settle material spending trade-offs, funding assumptions and delegated limits. Capture what directors approved, requested changes to or deferred, including conditions and follow-up decisions. Apply agreed revisions to the model and distinguish the plan discussed from the version that will receive formal approval.

execution.rationale: Directors discuss and settle plan conditions in the board's chosen meeting process.

parts.title: Board signs the consent approving the budget
parts.guidance: Prepare the budget consent under the company’s governing documents, identifying the final model, approval scope, spending limits and conditions. The required directors review and sign through the applicable corporate process. Link the executed resolution to the adopted budget and communicate its limits to finance so spending authority follows the actual decision.

execution.rationale: The required directors personally sign the budget consent through the company's applicable process, whose medium is unspecified.

metadata.supportReason: Pulling actuals and drafting the model are automatable; the department trade-offs and the board vote are judgment, and the board consent is a signed corporate act.
